raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

This change adds a new secondary tier pair, valkey and
valkey-large-object, next to the fs and obj tiers.

The valkey provider uses plain get/set through valkey-glide, and
valkey-large-object uses RDMA over efa-direct. The new module is
valkey-io/valkey-large-object.

In preliminary time-to-first-token tests using an RTX Pro 4500
Blackwell with Qwen3-8B-FP8 and a 15k token prompt, plain
valkey (4056ms) is slower than GPU recompute (1809ms). However,
valkey-large-object (359ms) is close to local NVMe (329ms).

I lifted the thread pool to tiering, and the job bookkeeping into
a shared PooledTierManager. The fs and both valkey tiers now
consume these components. The fs test helpers also moved to
pooled_tier_utils.py so the new tier tests can share them.

https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey-large-object

## Claims

Extends the tiering infrastructure to support Valkey. While Valkey itself
over tcp does not look particularly compelling, the RDMA path through
valkey-large-object appears competitive with local ssd, with attendant
pros and cons to shared remote KV cache.

## Validation

An end-to-end time to first token test was chosen to get a first
approximation of performance. KV caches were flushed between runs to
make it relatively fair, and the deltas are large enough to at least show
the form of the change.

Model choice was based on convenience and fit for the hardware I was
able to get. There will definitely be a different prefill:load break-even point
on different hardware - and on different network interfaces.

```
Median request latency (max_tokens=1), Qwen3-8B-FP8 on g7.8xlarge
(RTX PRO 4500), valkey on c8gn.16xl, 3 runs per cell:
  ┌─────────────────────┬───────────┬─────────┬─────────┐
  │       Source        │ 2k tokens │ 8k      │ 15k     │
  ├─────────────────────┼───────────┼─────────┼─────────┤
  │ cold prefill        │ 168 ms    │ 799 ms  │ 1809 ms │
  ├─────────────────────┼───────────┼─────────┼─────────┤
  │ GPU prefix cache    │ 20 ms     │ 31 ms   │ 45 ms   │
  ├─────────────────────┼───────────┼─────────┼─────────┤
  │ host memory         │ 31 ms     │ 61 ms   │ 94 ms   │
  │ (CPU tier)          │           │         │         │
  ├─────────────────────┼───────────┼─────────┼─────────┤
  │ local NVMe          │ 64 ms     │ 187 ms  │ 329 ms  │
  │ (fs, O_DIRECT)      │           │         │         │
  ├─────────────────────┼───────────┼─────────┼─────────┤
  │ valkey-large-object │ 67 ms     │ 198 ms  │ 359 ms  │
  │ (efa)               │           │         │         │
  ├─────────────────────┼───────────┼─────────┼─────────┤
  │ plain Valkey        │ 553 ms    │ 2168 ms │ 4056 ms │
  └─────────────────────┴───────────┴─────────┴─────────┘
```

### To reproduce:
First, recognize this is a module under active development and client releases are being worked on. With that said,

#### vllm
* Build [the WIP glide-sync client](https://github.com/anitarua/valkey-glide/tree/feat/rdma-4-python-sync) with GLIDE_SYNC_RDMA=1
* Generate the `glide_shared/protobuf` pb2 modules with protoc, because glide source doesn't include them.
* Install libfabric, either from the EFA installer or a libfabric package if you use the tcp provider. (Or use an instance with libfabric already installed on the system)

#### valkey-large-object
Build the module https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey-large-object
```
valkey-server --save "" \
    --loadmodule libvalkey_large_object.so operating-mode Dram dram-maxmemory 4gb
```

```
VLLM_TEST_VALKEY_LARGE_OBJECT_NODES=127.0.0.1:6379 \
    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_valkey_large_object_tier.py -v
```

## Details

The valkey-large-object project is very new, and currently inconvenient to use. But over the coming months,
the glide client will be updated and the module will have releases. RDMA-capable hardware and specialty
networking is required to make the most of this secondary tier. For users on AWS, there is some choice there,
and support for other RDMA hardware is planned.

+### Valkey
+
+The Valkey tier (`type: "valkey"`) stores each chunk as a string key on a Valkey server or cluster through [valkey-glide-sync](https://pypi.org/project/valkey-glide-sync/) (`pip install valkey-glide-sync`). Stores `SET` straight from the CPU KV cache and loads `GET` straight into it.

+| Key | Required | Default | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `type` | yes | — | Must be `valkey`. |
+| `startup_nodes` | yes | — | Comma-separated `host:port` seed nodes. |

+| `timeout_ms` | no | `5000` | Per-request timeout; size it for one chunk. |
+| `n_read_threads` | no | `16` | Read-priority I/O threads (load path). |
+| `n_write_threads` | no | `16` | Write-priority I/O threads (store path). |
+| `enable_kv_events` | no | `false` | Publish `BlockStored` KV events (medium `STORAGE`) for successfully stored blocks. Requires KV cache events to be enabled globally. |
+| `locality` | no | unspecified | `LOCAL` or `REMOTE` relative to the publishing vLLM instance. Included in the tier's KV events only when explicitly configured. |
+
+```json
+"secondary_tiers": [{
+  "type": "valkey",
+  "startup_nodes": "kv.internal:6379",
+  "cluster_mode": true,
+  "ttl_seconds": 3600
+}]
+```
+
+Keys are `<key_prefix>/<type>/` followed by the filesystem tier's layout (see [On-Disk Layout](#on-disk-layout)), so the [Cross-Process Sharing](#cross-process-sharing) behavior applies to instances sharing a Valkey. vLLM does not evict from Valkey: set `ttl_seconds`, or configure `maxmemory` with an eviction `maxmemory-policy` on the server. A chunk evicted between lookup and load fails that load and is recomputed. At startup the tier writes its run configuration to `<key_prefix>/<type>/<model>_<digest>/config.json` and fails fast if the server is unreachable.
+
+### Valkey Large Object
+
+The Valkey large-object tier (`type: "valkey-large-object"`) stores chunks with the [valkey-large-object](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey-large-object) module and moves them by RDMA: the CPU KV cache is registered once and the server reads and writes it directly. It requires an RDMA-enabled build of valkey-glide-sync and libfabric. It accepts every [Valkey](#valkey) key plus:
+
+| Key | Required | Default | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `type` | yes | — | Must be `valkey-large-object`. |
+| `rdma_provider` | no | `efa-direct` | `efa-direct`, or `tcp` for RDMA emulated over TCP (development and CI). |
+| `rdma_interface` | no | first | Fabric domain to pin to when a host has more than one. |
+| `rdma_region_bytes` | no | `16777216` (16 MiB) | Target size of each registered RDMA region, rounded down to whole chunks (at least one). |
+| `timeout_ms` | no | `5000` | Deadline for one chunk transfer. |
+
+The CPU KV cache is registered as consecutive regions of about `rdma_region_bytes`, so registered memory totals one copy of the cache. A region serves one transfer at a time: transfers to chunks in different regions run in parallel, and transfers within a region take turns. Smaller regions allow more parallelism at the cost of more registrations, which count against the fabric's limit on the number of memory registrations.
+
+RDMA transfers cannot time out on their own. When a transfer overruns `timeout_ms` or the connection fails, the tier closes the client, which cancels every in-flight transfer and revokes the server's access to the CPU KV cache, then reconnects and registers the cache again. The cancelled transfers fail and their chunks are recomputed.
+
 ### P2P (Including P/D)
 
 The P2P tier (`type: "p2p"`) shares completed KV blocks between vLLM instances over RDMA via NIXL. Each instance binds a control socket on `host:port` and exchanges blocks directly with peers — no shared filesystem required.

+"""In-memory Valkey clients for the valkey tier tests."""
+
+import threading
+import time
+from collections import defaultdict, deque
+
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.valkey_large_object.client import (

+class FakeValkeyClient:
+    """In-memory ValkeyClient. Exceptions queued in ``failures[operation]``
+    are raised by the next calls to that operation.
+
+    Clients built over the same ``values`` see the same server data, as a
+    reconnected client would.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, values: dict[str, bytes] | None = None) -> None:
+        self.values: dict[str, bytes] = {} if values is None else values
+        self.ttls: dict[str, int | None] = {}
+        self.failures: defaultdict[str, deque[Exception]] = defaultdict(deque)
+        self.closed = False
+
+    def _raise_queued_failure(self, operation: str) -> None:
+        if self.failures[operation]:
+            raise self.failures[operation].popleft()
+
+    def set(self, key: str, value: memoryview, ttl_seconds: int | None) -> None:
+        self._raise_queued_failure("set")
+        self.values[key] = bytes(value)
+        self.ttls[key] = ttl_seconds
+
+    def get_into(self, key: str, buffer: memoryview) -> int | None:
+        self._raise_queued_failure("get")
+        value = self.values.get(key)
+        if value is None:
+            return None
+        if len(buffer) < len(value):
+            raise ValueError("value larger than buffer")
+        buffer[: len(value)] = value
+        return len(value)
+
+    def exists_each(self, keys: list[str]) -> list[bool]:
+        return [key in self.values for key in keys]
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.closed = True
+
+
+class FakeLargeObjectClient(FakeValkeyClient):
+    """In-memory LargeObjectClient.
+
+    As in glide, a region serves one transfer at a time: a transfer on a busy
+    region records the violation in ``overlapping_transfers`` and fails.
+    ``transfer_seconds`` stretches transfers so overlaps would show. With
+    ``hang_transfers`` set, transfers block until ``close()`` cancels them.
+    ``events`` records region lifecycle and cancellation order.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, values: dict[str, bytes] | None = None) -> None:
+        super().__init__(values)
+        self.regions: list[memoryview] = []
+        self.hang_transfers = False
+        self.transfer_seconds = 0.0
+        self.overlapping_transfers = 0
+        self.events: list[str] = []
+        self._busy: set[int] = set()
+        self._busy_lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._closed = threading.Event()
+
+    def register_region(self, memory: memoryview) -> int:
+        self.regions.append(memory.cast("B"))
+        self.events.append("register_region")
+        return len(self.regions) - 1
+

+"""PooledTierManager: shared job bookkeeping for secondary tiers whose
+transfers are blocking calls run on a DualQueueThreadPool.
+
+Subclasses build one task per job (a callable that moves every chunk of the
+job) and an AsyncLookupManager; this base class tracks the jobs, keeps the
+prefix of a partially failed load, and emits KV events for successful stores.
+
+A load task that fails part-way raises an exception carrying
+``num_succeeded``, the number of chunks loaded before the failing one, so
+those chunks are kept in the primary tier.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, ClassVar
+
+from typing_extensions import override
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import (
+    Locality,
+    LookupResult,
+    Medium,
+    OffloadingEvent,
+    OffloadKey,
+    ReqContext,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.async_lookup import AsyncLookupManager
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.backpressure import BackpressureDetector
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.base import (
+    JobId,
+    JobResult,
+    RequestOffloadingContext,
+    ScheduleEndContext,
+    SecondaryTierManager,
+    TransferJob,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.thread_pool import DualQueueThreadPool
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import OffloadingSpec
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class PartialLoadError(Exception):
+    """A load task failed after loading its first ``num_succeeded`` chunks."""
+
+    def __init__(self, num_succeeded: int) -> None:
+        super().__init__(f"load failed after {num_succeeded} chunks")
+        self.num_succeeded = num_succeeded
+
+
+class PooledTierManager(SecondaryTierManager):
+    """Secondary tier running one blocking task per job on a thread pool.
+
+    Read-priority threads service load jobs preferentially; write-priority
+    threads service store jobs preferentially.  Both groups can drain either
+    queue, so neither starves.
+
+    Subclasses must assign ``self._lookup_manager`` in their ``__init__``.
+    """
+
+    medium: ClassVar[Medium] = Medium.STORAGE
+
+    _lookup_manager: AsyncLookupManager
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        offloading_spec: "OffloadingSpec",
+        primary_kv_view: memoryview,
+        tier_type: str,
+        n_read_threads: int,
+        n_write_threads: int,
+        thread_name_prefix: str,
+        enable_kv_events: bool = False,
+        locality: str | None = None,
+        backpressure_detector: BackpressureDetector | None = None,
+    ):
+        """Args:
+        offloading_spec: Contains normalized offloading configuration and
+            blocks_per_chunk.
+        primary_kv_view: Memoryview of the primary tier's CPU KV cache.
+        tier_type: Tier type identifier, set by SecondaryTierFactory.
+        n_read_threads: Number of read-priority I/O threads.
+        n_write_threads: Number of write-priority I/O threads.
+        thread_name_prefix: Name prefix for the pool's threads.
+        enable_kv_events: Emit BlockStored KV events for blocks
+            successfully stored to this tier. Effective only when KV
+            cache events are enabled globally (kv_events_config).
+        locality: Whether this tier's storage is LOCAL or REMOTE relative
+            to the publishing vLLM instance.
+        backpressure_detector: Optional backpressure detector.
+
+        """
+        super().__init__(
+            offloading_spec, primary_kv_view, tier_type, backpressure_detector
+        )
+        self.locality = Locality(locality) if locality is not None else None
+
+        self.events: list[OffloadingEvent] | None = None
+        if enable_kv_events:
+            if offloading_spec.kv_events_config.enable_kv_cache_events:
+                self.events = []
+            else:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "enable_kv_events is set on secondary tier '%s' but KV "
+                    "cache events are disabled globally; the tier will not "
+                    "emit events.",
+                    tier_type,
+                )
+        # Keys of in-flight store jobs, tracked only when events are enabled.
+        self._store_job_keys: dict[JobId, list[OffloadKey]] = {}
+        # Keys of in-flight load (promotion) jobs, so a failed load can mark
+        # its own cached lookup verdicts False (see get_finished_jobs).
+        self._load_job_keys: dict[JobId, list[OffloadKey]] = {}
+        # Block count per in-flight job, used to report transfer_bytes.
+        self._job_block_counts: dict[JobId, int] = {}
+        # Per load job: how many blocks loaded before a failure (partial keep).
+        # Written by the pool worker inside the load task before it raises (so
+        # before task_done publishes the job); read on the scheduler thread in
+        # get_finished_jobs only for job ids the finished queue returned. Under
+        # the GIL that read cannot observe the finished job without the prior
+        # write, so no extra lock is needed (get_finished is itself lock-free).
+        self._load_progress: dict[JobId, int] = {}
+
+        self._pool = DualQueueThreadPool(
+            n_read_threads,
+            n_write_threads,
+            thread_name_prefix=thread_name_prefix,
+        )
+
+    def _chunk_offsets(self, job_metadata: TransferJob) -> list[int]:
+        """Byte offset in the primary view of each chunk in the job."""
+        return [int(cid) * self._block_size_bytes for cid in job_metadata.chunk_ids]
+
+    def _enqueue_store(
+        self, job_metadata: TransferJob, task: Callable[[], None]
+    ) -> None:
+        if self.events is not None:
+            self._store_job_keys[job_metadata.job_id] = list(job_metadata.keys)
+        self._job_block_counts[job_metadata.job_id] = len(job_metadata.keys)
+        self._pool.enqueue_store(job_metadata.job_id, 1, [task])
+
+    def _enqueue_load(
+        self, job_metadata: TransferJob, task: Callable[[], None]
+    ) -> None:
+        job_id = job_metadata.job_id
+        # Track this load's keys so a failed promotion can mark only its failed
+        # keys as a miss (see get_finished_jobs).
+        keys = list(job_metadata.keys)
+        self._load_job_keys[job_id] = keys
+        self._job_block_counts[job_id] = len(keys)
+
+        def load_task() -> None:
+            try:
+                task()
+            except Exception as exc:
+                # Runs on the pool worker thread. Record how many blocks loaded
+                # before the failure so get_finished_jobs can keep them; this
+                # write precedes task_done, so the scheduler reads it safely
+                # under the GIL once the finished queue hands back this job.
+                num_succeeded = getattr(exc, "num_succeeded", 0)
+                self._load_progress[job_id] = num_succeeded
+                logger.debug(
+                    "Load of %d blocks for job %s failed at block %d: %s",
+                    len(keys),
+                    job_id,
+                    num_succeeded,
+                    exc,
+                )
+                raise
+
+        self._pool.enqueue_load(job_id, 1, [load_task])
+
+    @override
+    def on_new_request(self, req_context: ReqContext) -> RequestOffloadingContext:
+        return RequestOffloadingContext()
+
+    @override
+    def lookup(self, key: OffloadKey, req_context: ReqContext) -> LookupResult:
+        result = self._lookup_manager.lookup(key, req_context)
+        if result is None:
+            return LookupResult.RETRY
+        return LookupResult.HIT if result else LookupResult.MISS
+
+    @override
+    def get_finished_jobs(self) -> Iterable[JobResult]:
+        """Collect finished jobs; a failed promotion marks only its failed keys
+        as a miss here (scheduler thread)."""
+        results = []
+        for job_id, success, transfer_time in self._pool.get_finished():
+            block_count = self._job_block_counts.pop(job_id, 0)
+            transfer_bytes = (
+                block_count * self._block_size_bytes if block_count else None
+            )
+            if self.events is not None:
+                keys = self._store_job_keys.pop(job_id, None)
+                if success and keys:
+                    self.events.append(
+                        OffloadingEvent(
+                            keys=keys,
+                            medium=self.medium,
+                            removed=False,
+                            locality=self.locality,
+                        )
+                    )
+            load_keys = self._load_job_keys.pop(job_id, None)
+            num_succeeded = self._load_progress.pop(job_id, 0)
+            if load_keys is not None and not success:
+                # A batched load stops at the first bad block and reports how
+                # many loaded before it. Those earlier blocks are kept in the
+                # primary tier (reported via successful_keys); only this block
+                # and the ones after it are marked a miss and recomputed.
+                successful = load_keys[:num_succeeded]
+                failed = load_keys[num_succeeded:]
+                self._lookup_manager.mark_miss(failed)
+                results.append(
+                    JobResult(
+                        job_id=job_id,
+                        success=False,
+                        successful_keys=tuple(successful) if successful else None,
+                        transfer_time=transfer_time,
+                        transfer_bytes=transfer_bytes,
+                    )
+                )
+                continue
+            results.append(
+                JobResult(
+                    job_id=job_id,
+                    success=success,
+                    transfer_time=transfer_time,
+                    transfer_bytes=transfer_bytes,
+                )
+            )
+        return results
+
+    @override
+    def take_events(self) -> Iterable[OffloadingEvent]:
+        if self.events is not None:
+            yield from self.events
+            self.events.clear()
+
+    @override
+    def drain_jobs(self) -> None:
+        """Block until all in-flight transfers in the threadpool finish."""
+        self._pool.wait_idle()
+
+    @override
+    def on_request_finished(self, req_context: ReqContext) -> None:
+        self._lookup_manager.cleanup(req_context.req_id)
+
+    @override
+    def on_schedule_end(self, context: ScheduleEndContext) -> None:
+        self._lookup_manager.flush()
+
+    @override
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        """Release resources held by this tier.
+
+        Shuts down the lookup manager and the thread pool,
+        clearing pending tasks and waiting for active threads to complete.
+        """
+        self._lookup_manager.shutdown()
+        self._pool.shutdown(wait=True)

+    for node in startup_nodes.split(","):
+        host, _, port = node.strip().rpartition(":")
+        if not host or not port.isdigit():

+class GlideValkeyClient:
+    """Thread-safe: one instance is shared by every pool thread."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        startup_nodes: str,
+        cluster_mode: bool,
+        timeout_ms: int,
+        **configuration_options: Any,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Args:
+        startup_nodes: Comma-separated ``host:port`` seed nodes.
+        cluster_mode: Connect as a cluster client.
+        timeout_ms: Glide request timeout.
+        configuration_options: Extra glide client configuration fields.
+        """
+        addresses = parse_startup_nodes(startup_nodes)
+        self._client: GlideClient | GlideClusterClient
+        self._batch_type: type[Batch] | type[ClusterBatch]
+        if cluster_mode:
+            self._client = GlideClusterClient.create(
+                GlideClusterClientConfiguration(
+                    addresses, request_timeout=timeout_ms, **configuration_options
+                )
+            )
+            self._batch_type = ClusterBatch
+        else:
+            self._client = GlideClient.create(
+                GlideClientConfiguration(
+                    addresses, request_timeout=timeout_ms, **configuration_options
+                )
+            )
+            self._batch_type = Batch
+

+        expiry = None if ttl_seconds is None else ExpirySet(ExpiryType.SEC, ttl_seconds)
+        self._client.set(key, value, expiry=expiry)
+
+    def get_into(self, key: str, buffer: memoryview) -> int | None:
+        # With a buffer, glide returns the byte count as a decimal string.
+        written = self._client.get(key, buffer=buffer)
+        return None if written is None else int(written)

+        # One EXISTS per key: a multi-key EXISTS returns only a count.
+        batch = self._batch_type(is_atomic=False)

+        return [bool(result) for result in results]

+"""ValkeyLargeObjectTierManager: KV cache offloading to Valkey with the
+valkey-large-object module, moving chunks by RDMA.
+
+The primary view is registered as disjoint RDMA regions of about
+``rdma_region_bytes`` each, covering whole chunks; each transfer is a window of
+its chunk's region, so the server reads and writes the CPU KV cache directly.
+A glide region serves one transfer at a time, so each region has a lock and
+transfers to chunks in different regions run in parallel. Registered memory
+totals one copy of the primary view.
+
+RDMA transfers have no timeout and can only be cancelled by closing the
+client. A watchdog thread closes the client when a transfer overruns
+``timeout_ms`` or the transport fails, then registers a fresh client.
+"""

+import time
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, TypeVar

+    """One client and its registered regions, replaced as a unit."""
+
+    __slots__ = ("client", "failed", "torn_down", "in_flight", "condition")
+
+    def __init__(self, client: LargeObjectClient) -> None:
+        self.client = client
+        # Set once a transfer fails or overruns; new transfers fail fast.
+        self.failed = False
+        self.torn_down = False

+        cluster_mode: bool = False,

+        offloading_spec: Contains normalized offloading configuration and
+            blocks_per_chunk.
+        primary_kv_view: Memoryview of the primary tier's CPU KV cache.
+        tier_type: Tier type identifier, set by SecondaryTierFactory.
+        startup_nodes: Comma-separated ``host:port`` seed nodes.
+        rdma_provider: ``"efa-direct"``, or ``"tcp"`` for RDMA emulated over
+            TCP (development and CI).
+        rdma_interface: Fabric domain to pin to when a host has several.
+        rdma_region_bytes: Target size of each registered region, rounded
+            down to whole chunks (at least one). Smaller regions allow more
+            parallel transfers at the cost of more registrations.
+        cluster_mode: Connect as a cluster client.
+        key_prefix: Prefix for every key this tier writes.
+        ttl_seconds: Expire stored chunks after this many seconds.
+        timeout_ms: Deadline for one chunk transfer; an overrun reconnects.
+        n_read_threads: Number of read-priority I/O threads.
+        n_write_threads: Number of write-priority I/O threads.
+        enable_kv_events: Emit BlockStored KV events for blocks
+            successfully stored to this tier. Effective only when KV
+            cache events are enabled globally (kv_events_config).
+        locality: Whether this tier's storage is LOCAL or REMOTE relative
+            to the publishing vLLM instance.
+        backpressure_detector: Optional backpressure detector.

+        self._rdma_provider = rdma_provider
+        self._rdma_interface = rdma_interface

+        chunk_bytes = primary_kv_view.strides[0]

+        num_regions = -(-primary_kv_view.nbytes // self._region_bytes)

+            target=self._watch, name="vllm_kv_lo_watch", daemon=True
+        )

+        from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.valkey_large_object.glide_client import (
+            GlideLargeObjectClient,
+        )

+        client = GlideLargeObjectClient(
+            self._startup_nodes,
+            self._cluster_mode,
+            self._timeout_ms,

+            self._rdma_interface,
+        )

+        return client

+                    transport.failed = True

+            finally:
+                with transport.condition:
+                    del transport.in_flight[thread]
+                    transport.condition.notify_all()
+
+    @override
+    def _store_chunk(self, key: str, offset: int) -> None:
+        self._transfer(
+            offset,
+            lambda client, region, region_offset: client.rdma_set(
+                key, region, region_offset, self._block_size_bytes
+            ),
+        )
+        if self._ttl_seconds is not None:
+            # The chunk is stored; without a TTL it lives until Valkey evicts it.
+            try:
+                self._transport.client.expire(key, self._ttl_seconds)
+            except Exception as error:
+                logger.debug("EXPIRE %s failed: %s", key, error)
+
+    @override
+    def _load_chunk(self, key: str, offset: int) -> bool:
+        written = self._transfer(
+            offset,
+            lambda client, region, region_offset: client.rdma_get(
+                key, region, region_offset, self._block_size_bytes
+            ),
+        )
+        return written == self._block_size_bytes
+
+    def _watch(self) -> None:
+        timeout = self._timeout_ms / 1000
+        while not self._stopping.is_set():
+            self._wake_watchdog.wait(timeout / 4)
+            self._wake_watchdog.clear()
+            if self._stopping.is_set():
+                return
+            transport = self._transport
+            with transport.condition:
+                now = time.monotonic()
+                overdue = any(
+                    timeout < now - start for start in transport.in_flight.values()
+                )
+                if not (transport.failed or overdue):
+                    continue
+                transport.failed = True
+            self._replace(transport)
+
+    def _replace(self, transport: _Transport) -> None:
+        if not transport.torn_down:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Valkey large-object tier '%s': a transfer failed or exceeded "
+                "%d ms; reconnecting.",
+                self.tier_type,
+                self._timeout_ms,
+            )
+            self._tear_down(transport)
+        try:
+            client = self._create_client()
+        except Exception as error:
+            # Retried on the next tick; transfers fail fast until then.
+            logger.debug("Reconnecting to %s failed: %s", self._startup_nodes, error)
+            return
+        self.client = client
+        self._transport = _Transport(client)
+
+    def _tear_down(self, transport: _Transport) -> None:
+        # Closing revokes the region before blocked transfers return, so the
+        # server cannot write into chunks the primary tier reclaims after their
+        # jobs fail.
+        transport.client.close()
+        with transport.condition:
+            transport.condition.wait_for(lambda: not transport.in_flight)
+        transport.client.release_regions()
+        transport.torn_down = True
+
+    @override
+    def _close_client(self) -> None:
+        # Runs after the pool has drained, with the watchdog still able to
+        # cancel a hung transfer during that drain.
+        self._stopping.set()
+        self._wake_watchdog.set()
+        self._watchdog.join()
+        if not self._transport.torn_down:
+            self._tear_down(self._transport)
